newsitem.title: FRANCE: DASA seeks to reassure Aerospatiale on Thomson bid.
newsitem.headline: DASA seeks to reassure Aerospatiale on Thomson bid.

text.p: The head of Daimler Benz Aerospace (DASA) said on Thursday long-time ally Aerospatiale had nothing to fear from its move to team up with Lagardere in bidding for French defence electronics group Thomson-CSF.
DASA's chairman told French newspaper Le Monde that Aerospatiale's worries that its Airbus partners, DASA and British Aerospace, would marginalise it within the Airbus consortium were unfounded.
British Aerospace is also backing Lagardere's bid.

"How could one believe we are trying to isolate Aerospatiale?" said Manfred Bischoff, chairman of DASA, which derives much of its turnover from joint activities with state-owned Aerospatiale, France's biggest aerospace group.
"Any move to marginalise (Aerospatiale) would rebound and weaken us," he said.

The alliance with missiles-to-publishing group Lagardere involved "well-defined sectors, outside more important areas of our collaboration with Aerospatiale" covering civilian planemaker Airbus, Eurocopter and Euromissiles, he said.
"Our friendship (DASA and Aerospatiale) goes back a long way. We will stay friends. That's clear," Bischoff said.
DASA threw its weight behind Lagardere's bid for state-controlled Thomson-CSF last week as it announced a strategic cooperation deal with Lagardere in space, missiles and defence electronics.
The move pitted it against Aerospatiale's support for a bid led by industrial giant Alcatel Alsthom.
After DASA's announcement, Aerospatiale head Yves Michot warned any move to "ally against Aerospatiale would be to sign the death warrant of Airbus".
He added that if the Lagardere-DASA-BAe consortium won Thomson-CSF, it could weaken the French aerospace industry and make it impossible to reorganise Airbus into a public company.
The other Airbus partner is Construcciones Aeronauticas of Spain which has not allied with any of the Thomson bidders.
Aerospatiale, whose interests range from commercial airliners and missiles to satellites, helicopters and regional turboprop planes, is not allowed to take part in the Thomson-CSF sale.
But Dassault Industries, parent of combat plane maker Dassault Aviation with which Aerospatiale plans to merge before its own privatisation this year, is bidding for Thomson-CSF with Alcatel.
"To see our ally of 30 years intervening in (the Thomson) sale in which we ourselves have not been able to participate leads us to pose certain questions," Michot said.

Lagardere chairman Noel Forgeard Lagardere denied separately that the alliance with DASA, a unit of German auto giant Daimler Benz, threatened Aerospatiale, which has been wooing DASA for years to form joint ventures in space and missiles.
"We hope to make concrete proposals for cooperation with Aerospatiale," he told the Le Figaro newspaper.

Bischoff said DASA joined forces with Lagardere to be able to tackle "growing competition from giant U.S. conglomerates born of the mergers of Lockheed-Martin, Boeing McDonnell Douglas or Raytheon Hughes," said Bischoff.
Lagardere's plans for Thomson-CSF represent the "best strategy for European success against the U.S. threat," he said.
-- Penny MacRae, Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
